transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-07-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Nina Kapoor (Vertex Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Vertex Security), Marta Reyes (Vertex ML Infra)

Summary:
Quick orientation focused on Redwood Console 'Request Capture Switchboard' (our internal name for the combined request storage / telemetry toggles) covering API + Console controls, Optimize recommendations for batching/redaction, and pilot next steps. Customer concerned about PII leakage, long-term telemetry retention, KMS integration and whether hosted vs dedicated affects egress and latency.

Topics: console tour, API flags, ephemeral vs persistent capture, PII redaction, KMS/HSM, RBAC & SSO, pilot measurement plan

[00:00:05] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Sofia, AE on the Redwood Inference platform. we've got Ethan from SE here, and we met with Nina and team, thanks for time.
[00:00:18] Nina Kapoor: Hi all, thanks. we're evaluating options for instrumenting our agent platform, we want to see how request capture and retention controls look end-to-end.
[00:00:27] Ethan Liu: Great. high level today — short console orientation, cover API toggles, show how Optimize suggests retention/batching settings, then talk pilot. any must-have items upfront?
[00:00:39] Liam O'Connor: Must-haves - SOC2 type2, KMS integration, ability to egress logs on customer network or ensure no exfil if hosted. also need to know what is redacted automatically vs what we have to configure.
[00:00:53] Sofia Martinez: Totally. we'll surface the SOC2 link and the privacy whitepaper in the follow-up. Ethan will show the console and the API flags for capture and redaction.

[00:01:12] Ethan Liu: Alright sharing screen — console, top nav - Observability -> Request Capture. this is our "switchboard" view, shows policies by route, retention TTL, and redaction rules.
[00:01:28] [00:01:29] Ethan Liu: so here you can toggle Request Storage: Off / Ephemeral / Persisted. Ephemeral keeps the request bodies for X minutes (configurable), Persisted stores them in customer bucket (if Dedicated/Private) or Redwood-managed encrypted store (if Hosted).
[00:01:45] Marta Reyes: quick q — when it's persisted in hosted, is the data encrypted with our key or Redwood key?
[00:01:51] Ethan Liu: Good question. Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default, but you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS for Dedicated and Private—BYOK for hosted is on the roadmap but not GA. there are audit logs showing key operations.
[00:02:08] Nina Kapoor: Can we configure per-route rules? We have some routes that touch SSNs and others that are safe.
[00:02:15] Ethan Liu: Yes — per-route policies. you can attach a redaction profile to a route: full redact, token-mask, or selective field ejection. I'll walk through a sample.
[00:02:26] [00:02:30] Ethan Liu: (narrating) here's the redaction policy editor — we ship some templates: PII-basic (email/phone/ssn), pii-extended (creditcard, driver license), and you can add custom regexes. rules are evaluated in order; we also have a safe-sample toggle so you can audit before enforcement.
[00:02:47] Liam O'Connor: And do those regexes run server-side before storage? like inline before it hits disk?
[00:02:54] Ethan Liu: Yes, inline — we run redaction in the ingress path. we do synchronous redaction so sensitive tokens never get written to persistent storage. ephemeral snapshots are kept in memory-managed caches and evicted according to TTL.
[00:03:08] Nina Kapoor: what's the overhead? does it add latency to requests?
[00:03:12] Ethan Liu: There is minimal overhead — we've optimized common regexes with compiled finite-state checks and we run redaction in parallel with batching where possible. expect small p50 delta (single-digit ms) on typical routes. for strict latency SLOs you can turn capture off for that route.
[00:03:29] [00:03:30] Sofia Martinez: this is where the tradeoff question comes in — latency vs observability. we advise instrumenting critical paths with ephemeral capture first then graduate to persisted for lower-volume async routes.

[00:03:50] Marta Reyes: For the ML infra angle, how does KV cache interact with request capture? if we store request/response for debugging, does it blow up the kv cache?
[00:03:59] Ethan Liu: Request storage is orthogonal to KV cache — KV remains model internals. we do not persist KV cache in the request store. we store request metadata and the cleared/redacted prompt/response pair. cache size unaffected.
[00:04:12] [00:04:18] Ethan Liu: also Optimize can recommend turning off prefix storage for high-cardinality routes to reduce storage and improve cache hits.

[00:04:30] Nina Kapoor: On dedicated versus hosted — if we go Dedicated does data ever touch Redwood-managed storage? we want physical isolation.
[00:04:39] Sofia Martinez: With Dedicated, you get dedicated GPU pools and option to configure storage to your cloud account (we support s3-compatible destinations). Private on-prem gives you full control — no Redwood-managed persistent stores.
[00:04:52] Liam O'Connor: Good. and networking? VPC peering, private link?
[00:04:56] Ethan Liu: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink for dedicated and private modes. for hosted, we do TLS in transit and can support IP allowlists and webhooks to customer endpoints.

[00:05:12] [00:05:15] Nina Kapoor: Show me a demo of setting a retention TTL by route and a redaction profile.
[00:05:19] Ethan Liu: Sure. selecting route /agents/parse. retention modal — default 30 days, can set to 0 (never persist), ephemeral 15 minutes, etc. saving will create a policy and you can see effective rules in the policy matrix.
[00:05:34] [00:05:36] Ethan Liu: now I'll attach 'pii-basic' redaction and enable 'safe-sample' 100 records. that will store masked copies to let you run Evaluate and Optimize jobs.
[00:05:49] Marta Reyes: safe-sample meaning we store a sampled copy unredacted for review? that sounds risky.
[00:05:55] Ethan Liu: safe-sample is configurable. by default it stores masked redacted copies only. if you opt into unredacted sampling for debugging, we strongly recommend using Private or Dedicated with BYOK. we'll show logs and audit trails when that toggle is used.

[00:06:10] [00:06:12] Liam O'Connor: Let's talk audit logs — we need immutable write-once logs for compliance and chain-of-custody.
[00:06:18] Sofia Martinez: Audit logs are exported to your destination (s3/GCS) with object immutability options for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers can request log export to their endpoint. logs include actor, action, policy id, and redaction hash.

[00:06:35] Nina Kapoor: Does Redwood encrypt at rest with AES-256 and rotate keys?
[00:06:40] Ethan Liu: Yes AES-256 for rest, KMS integrations for key rotation. rotation events are surfaced in Audit. for Dedicated/Private you manage keys via BYOK.

[00:06:52] [00:07:00] Ethan Liu: Switching to API — there's an optional header X-Redwood-Capture set per request. it allows you to override default route policy for a single call (useful for debug). headers accepted: capture=on|off|ephemeral, redact=profile-name. note: we recommend batching debug traffic to avoid cost spikes.
[00:07:19] Nina Kapoor: Can we programmatically call Optimize recommendations via API? we'd like to automate cost recommendations.
[00:07:24] Ethan Liu: Yes Optimize has an API endpoint /optimize/recommendations that returns quantization and batching suggestions per workload sample. we'll send a postman snippet after. link will be in follow up: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/api#recommendations

[00:07:40] [00:07:45] Marta Reyes: Any built-in PII detection models or is it strictly regex? regex won't catch all patterns.
[00:07:51] Ethan Liu: We ship a hybrid stack — heuristic regex for common tokens and a lightweight NER-based PII detector for ambiguous cases. customers can bring custom models for on-prem. NER runs inline but in a reduced confidence mode to keep latency low. there's a configurable confidence threshold to block storage if detection probability high.

[00:08:15] Liam O'Connor: Good. are we able to run the PII detector locally in our environment?
[00:08:19] Sofia Martinez: In Private/on-prem we can deploy the detector in your environment, yes. for Dedicated you can request a private agent to run detection on your VPC.

[00:08:33] [00:08:40] Ethan Liu: Quick note on cost — persistent storage and long retention adds cost. Optimize can show estimated monthly cost for each TTL setting so you can tune. couple examples: keeping 90 days of 1M requests/month ~ ~ $X (placeholder) — we'll give a real estimate in the pilot spreadsheet.

[00:09:05] Nina Kapoor: ok show us the pilot plan. what does Redwood need from us to kick off a benchmark?
[00:09:11] Sofia Martinez: We'll need a representative traffic sample (anonymized), list of high-priority routes, desired SLOs, and the list of PII fields you want redacted or exempt. Ethan will supply a minimal script to replay requests and collect telemetry.
[00:09:23] [00:09:30] Ethan Liu: I'll also provide a small terraform snippet to wire up S3 export for Dedicated pilot, and a script to toggle capture headers for selective routes.

[00:09:42] Marta Reyes: timeline? we want to see numbers within two weeks.
[00:09:45] Sofia Martinez: We can do a 7-14 day benchmark window. propose start next week, run for 7 days, then analyze.

[00:09:58] [00:10:05] Liam O'Connor: On the legal side, we may want to see a DPA with specific retention limits — can you share template?
[00:10:12] Sofia Martinez: Yes will include DPA template, plus export of security artifacts.

[00:10:25] [00:10:40] Nina Kapoor: Another question — how do rollbacks interact with persisted request stores? if we rollback model versions, will stored requests still be tied to a model id?
[00:10:46] Ethan Liu: We persist metadata including model version and the runtime snapshot id. rollback doesn't delete historical requests unless you run a purge. retention policies govern lifecycle; you can set per-deployment retention independent of model lifecycle.

[00:11:05] [00:11:10] Ethan Liu: demo: showing Optimize recommendations for a route — using the sample traffic it suggests reducing max tokens 10% and enable 4-bit quantization for offline batch jobs, plus advice to switch ephemeral capture for this route to 1 hour TTL.
[00:11:26] Marta Reyes: quantization on open models is great but does it change outputs in a way that affects our regression tests?
[00:11:32] Ethan Liu: There's a small chance — Optimize will run evals and surface quality regression risk as a score. you can pin a model variant or configure fallback to a higher-precision model if quality drops beyond threshold.

[00:11:48] [00:12:00] Nina Kapoor: Ok let's surface security-specific items: SSO/SAML, RBAC, usage-level permissioning to control who can change capture settings.
[00:12:08] Sofia Martinez: Console supports SCIM + SAML for user provisioning. RBAC is granular: route-level policy editors, audit-only roles, and a 'security-admin' role required to flip retention to persisted. all changes are logged in audit trail and exportable.

[00:12:28] Liam O'Connor: Does RBAC cover API overrides like X-Redwood-Capture header? can we restrict it to service accounts only?
[00:12:34] Ethan Liu: Yes, you can define service accounts and token scopes. override headers require a token with 'capture:override' scope.

[00:12:44] [00:13:00] Nina Kapoor: Can you show the audit entry for a policy change?
[00:13:03] Ethan Liu: (narrating) here's a sample event: timestamp, actor, ip, policy-id, before/after diffs, and an HMAC'd redaction hash. you can export to your SIEM via webhook.

[00:13:20] Marta Reyes: About developer ergonomics — are there CLI tools or SDKs to manage capture?
[00:13:25] Ethan Liu: Yes — CLI (redwoodctl) has commands 'capture set' and 'capture test' and SDK methods in python/js. snippet will be shared.

[00:13:40] [00:14:00] Nina Kapoor: Any gotchas? have customers hit surprises?
[00:14:04] Sofia Martinez: A common gotcha: enabling unredacted safe-sample in hosted without proper key controls. We heavily recommend Dedicated or Private if you need unredacted debugging.

[00:14:20] Ethan Liu: Another: high-cardinality routes can blow up storage costs — Optimize flags high-cardinality tokens and suggests token masking or smaller safe-sample rates.

[00:14:34] [00:15:00] Questions from Vertex:
- How do we request purge and ejection of data on demand?
- What legal process is required for forensic access?
- How do we validate that redaction rules applied correctly?

[00:15:10] Sofia Martinez: Purge API available; you can request programmatic purge by retention-id and we return a sweep token. For forensic access we have a documented process and require authorized tickets plus audit trail. For validation, we have a sample-validation job that runs tests against a safe-sample and reports false negatives/positives.

[00:15:40] [00:16:00] Ethan Liu: demo: run a validation job — it reports 99.1% detection on the sample set with 0.2% false positives. notes: confidence threshold adjustable.

[00:16:22] Nina Kapoor: Great. let's talk about metrics we'll look at during the pilot — what telemetry should we collect?
[00:16:28] Ethan Liu: Latency p50/p95/p99, token usage, storage consumed by retention (GB/day), number of redaction hits, detection confidence histogram, and egress counts. we'll include these in the pilot dashboard.

[00:16:50] Marta Reyes: Any suggested knobs for reducing storage with minimal loss of observability?
[00:16:56] Ethan Liu: A few: turn on token-mask for emails, enable ephemeral 1hr for high-volume routes, use safe-sample 0.1%, compress persisted payloads via gzip, and use Optimize to move bulk async workloads to quantized batch endpoints.

[00:17:15] Sofia Martinez: Also note our SDK supports streaming redaction so clients can redact on-device before sending if you want client-side filtering.

[00:17:30] [00:18:00] Quick pause — check if we covered major points.
[00:18:07] Nina Kapoor: yes, this is helpful. we have two internal follow-up items: get legal review ready and prepare a small anonymized traffic dump.

[00:18:22] Sofia Martinez: Next steps recap — we'll send the whitepaper/DPA, the pilot config, and scripts. propose pilot start 2029-07-18.

[00:18:35] [00:19:00] Short technical Q&A (some cross talk):
[00:19:06] Liam O'Connor: Is there any way to keep a hash of original content to allow later verification without storing the content?
[00:19:12] Ethan Liu: Yes — we compute salted HMACs of raw values before redaction so you can verify matches without storing raw text. keys for HMAC are customer-managed in BYOK setups.

[00:19:30] Marta Reyes: When you say BYOK in Dedicated — how is the key lifecycle managed?
[00:19:35] Ethan Liu: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS/KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) — you configure key IDs and we perform envelope encryption with customer key. rotation handled by KMS.

[00:19:50] [00:20:00] Nina Kapoor: Do you support multiple retention buckets per region?
[00:20:04] Ethan Liu: Yes — you can map routes to buckets by region. for compliance you can pin a route to a regional store.

[00:20:18] Sofia Martinez: We're nearing the end — any blockers?
[00:20:22] Liam O'Connor: blockers: need to confirm legal terms and cost estimate for 90-day persisted retention on a set of 12 routes.
[00:20:31] Sofia Martinez: We'll include estimate in pilot sheet.

[00:20:40] [00:21:00] Closing demo bits — links and artifacts referenced:
- Security whitepaper: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/whitepaper.pdf
- SOC2 extract: (attached in follow-up)
- Pilot config template: https://docs.redwood.ai/pilot/templates/retention-pilot.yaml
- Optimize API docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/api#recommendations
- CLI snippet: redwoodctl capture set --route /agents/parse --retention ephemeral:1h --redact pii-basic

[00:21:34] Nina Kapoor: ok let's lock the pilot dates offline.
[00:21:38] Sofia Martinez: perfect. Ethan anything else to add?
[00:21:42] Ethan Liu: I'll make sure to include the terraform + replay script and a minimal set of test vectors. also will include steps to enable BYOK on Dedicated if you choose that path.

[00:21:55] [00:22:00] Misc conversation and minor interruptions (background noise). some words incorrectly transcribed: 'redaction' sometimes appears as 'reduction'.

[00:22:20] Final recap:
- Redwood to share security whitepaper, DPA, SOC2 extract.
- Redwood to provide pilot config, replay script, terraform snippet, and cost estimate.
- Vertex to provide anonymized traffic sample, list of routes, and PII field list.
- Schedule pilot kickoff (proposed 2029-07-18).

[00:22:45] End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional word swaps (reduction vs redaction), speaker labels may be simplified (Ethan sometimes labeled as Speaker 2 in export). timestamps are approximate.
